Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure, and repealing Directive 2014/94/EU» It is an EU regulation and applies in the European Union. It was published on 22 September 2023 («OJ L 234, 22.9.2023»). «The specific objectives of the Regulation are: to ensure minimum infrastructure to support the required uptake of alternative fuel vehicles across all transport modes and in all EU Member States to meet the EU’s climate objectives; to ensure full interoperability of the infrastructure; and to ensure comprehensive user information and adequate payment options at alternative fuels infrastructure.»

Statements of what the text requires are marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* where a freight forwarder's role is not named in the text; statements that go beyond the text are marked as analysis. *Analytical inference:* the date of the next scheduled review is the Commission review of this Regulation set out in Article 24, described in section 6.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets minimum recharging and refuelling infrastructure that each Member State has to deploy. The effective date is 13 April 2024: «The regulation is applicable since 13 April 2024.» «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» «The regulation sets a number of mandatory national targets for the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure in the EU, for road vehicles, vessels and stationary aircraft.»

For a freight forwarder it matters on three modes: heavy-duty road charging on the main EU road network, shore-side electricity for container ships in ports, and hydrogen refuelling. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the targets are addressed to Member States; no duty on a forwarder is stated, and the source states no effect on a forwarder. *Analytical inference:* the targets set where recharging infrastructure for road vehicles, vessels and stationary aircraft is deployed (claims 5 and 7), so a forwarder's exposure would run through the infrastructure its carriers can reach; the text does not say so. Effect by cargo vertical (live events, artwork, luxury goods, film and television, automotive, humanitarian) requires carrier-specific data and is not stated by this source.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no action falls within 30 days of the document date. The nearest dated step is the Commission review, which falls on a date about two months away. «By 31 December 2026 and every five years thereafter, the Commission shall review this Regulation.»

*Operational implication:* a regulatory lead who wants the forwarder's lane needs reflected in the review prepares a short position on the heavy-duty traffic thresholds before the end of 2026; the review assesses whether the traffic thresholds are still relevant and a possible extension of scope to other ship types, and the text does not say the targets will change.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty holders in the text are Member States and the operators and owners of recharging and refuelling points. «Member States shall ensure a minimum coverage of publicly accessible recharging points dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles in their territory.» «By 14 April 2025, operators of publicly accessible recharging points and refuelling points for alternative fuels, or, in accordance with the arrangements between them, the owners of those points, shall ensure the availability of static data and dynamic data»

A freight forwarder is not named. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that owns or operates its own depot charging counts as an operator for the data duty is not stated and should be confirmed with counsel; the source states no effect on a forwarder that buys road legs.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Two Commission reports are set in Article 24. The first, due by 31 December 2024, is past: «By 31 December 2024, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a technology and market-readiness report dedicated to heavy-duty vehicles.» The second is the review: «whether the traffic thresholds referred to in Article 3(6) and (7), in Article 4(4) and (5) and in Article 6(4) are still relevant»

*Analytical inference:* the traffic thresholds decide where the Member State derogations on heavy-duty charging pools apply, so a change in them would change which road sections must have the full pool power; the captured text does not say what the Commission will propose.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The heavy-duty charging targets are set by Article 4(1) in dated steps. Member States have to ensure each of the following.

- «(a) by 31 December 2025, along at least 15 % of the length of the TEN-T road network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel and that each recharging pool offers a power output of at least 1 400 kW and includes at least one recharging point with an individual power output of at least 350 kW;»
- «(b) by 31 December 2027, along at least 50 % of the length of the TEN-T road network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel and that each recharging pool: (i) along the TEN-T core road network, offers a power output of at least 2 800 kW and includes at least two recharging points with an individual power output of at least 350 kW; (ii) along the TEN-T comprehensive road network, offers a power output of at least 1 400 kW and includes at least one recharging point with an individual power output of at least 350 kW;»
- «(c) by 31 December 2030, along the TEN-T core road network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel with a maximum distance of 60 km between them and that each recharging pool offers a power output of at least 3 600 kW and includes at least two recharging points with an individual power output of at least 350 kW;»
- «(d) by 31 December 2030, along the TEN-T comprehensive road network, publicly accessible recharging pools dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles are deployed in each direction of travel with a maximum distance of 100 km between them and each recharging pool offers a power output of at least 1 500 kW and includes at least one recharging point with an individual power output of at least 350 kW;»
- «(e) by 31 December 2027, in each safe and secure parking area at least two publicly accessible recharging stations dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an individual power output of at least 100 kW are deployed;»
- «(f) by 31 December 2030, in each safe and secure parking area at least four publicly accessible recharging stations dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an individual power output of at least 100 kW are deployed;»
- «(g) by 31 December 2025, in each urban node publicly accessible recharging points dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an aggregated power output of at least 900 kW are deployed, provided by recharging stations with an individual power output of at least 150 kW;»
- «(h) by 31 December 2030, in each urban node publicly accessible recharging points dedicated to heavy-duty electric vehicles with an aggregated power output of at least 1 800 kW are deployed, provided by recharging stations with an individual power output of at least 150 kW.»

Derogations and method: «By way of derogation from paragraph 1 of this Article, along roads of the TEN-T network with a total annual average daily traffic of fewer than 2 000 heavy-duty vehicles and where the deployment of infrastructure cannot be justified in socio-economic cost-benefit terms» «The calculation of the percentage of the length of TEN-T road network referred to in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b), shall be based on the following elements»

Conditions and scope changes: «However, Member States should, subject to Union State aid rules, be able to support the deployment of the necessary publicly accessible recharging infrastructure» The review may also change scope: «a possible extension of the scope of this Regulation to other ship types following relevant adjustments in other relevant Union legal acts»

*Analytical inference:* the steps run end 2025, end 2027 and end 2030 and rise in power and in network coverage; the end-2025 step has passed, the end-2027 and end-2030 steps are ahead, and the text states no penalty for a Member State that misses a step.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Article 4(1) targets, points (a) to (h), are addressed to Member States; whether a given road section falls under the traffic-threshold derogation of Article 4, and whether a forwarder that operates its own depot charging has any duty under them, are questions for counsel.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 12.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties in the text sit with Member States and operators: «Member States shall review those cases every two years as part of the national progress reporting referred to in Article 15.» «By 14 April 2025, operators of publicly accessible recharging points and refuelling points for alternative fuels, or, in accordance with the arrangements between them, the owners of those points, shall ensure the availability of static data and dynamic data»

The penalty summary is a gap: the captured text states no penalty or sanction. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the national implementing rules and any enforcement route are outside the captured text.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the operational system requirement for a forwarder is a lane-planning field, not a system change.

- A procurement lead adds, at the next carrier onboarding round, to the road carrier onboarding form a field for the heavy-duty charging the carrier relies on and the TEN-T section it runs, so that coverage steps in Article 4 can be matched to the lane.
- A regulatory lead drafts, before 31 December 2026, the position on the Article 4 traffic thresholds named in section 3, for the review set in Article 24.

*Operational implication:* these two steps use only the dates the text states and no cost figure.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22 September 2023: the Regulation is published in the Official Journal
- 13 April 2024: the Regulation begins to apply
- 31 December 2025: first heavy-duty charging step, with pools along part of the TEN-T road network (date passed)
- 31 December 2026: Commission review of the Regulation
- 31 December 2027: second heavy-duty charging step, with wider network coverage
- 31 December 2030: third heavy-duty charging step, with pool spacing and power at full level
